title: On-Road Driving Test
examFocus: Road test — practice after you get your permit and start trucking school
summary: What examiners watch for on the road: turns, intersections, railroad crossings, and the general driving behaviors that get scored throughout.

topics.heading: The basics
bullets: Wear your seatbelt, obey every traffic law, and complete the route with zero accidents and zero moving violations.
If your route lacks a certain situation (like a railroad crossing), you may be asked to simulate it by explaining what you would do.

topics.heading: Turns & intersections
bullets: Check traffic in all directions, signal early, and don't coast unsafely (out of gear for longer than your vehicle's length).
Complete a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane; complete a left turn in the lane directly right of the center line on a multi-lane road.

topics.heading: Stop/start & roadside stop procedure
bullets: Signal, decelerate, and stop fully out of the traffic flow. Then: cancel the turn signal, activate 4-way flashers, set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and remove your feet from the pedals.
To resume: check traffic and mirrors, turn off flashers, signal left, release the parking brake, and pull out only once it's safe — don't turn the wheel before the vehicle starts moving.

topics.heading: Railroad crossings on the road test
bullets: Buses, school buses, and placarded vehicles must activate 4-way flashers approaching the crossing, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail, and look/listen both ways.
Never stop, shift gears, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the crossing.

topics.heading: General driving behaviors scored the whole route
bullets: Clutch usage (manual transmission): always use the clutch to shift, double-clutch on unsynchronized transmissions, never ride the clutch or 'pop' it.
Gear usage: no grinding or clashing gears, and don't shift while turning or in an intersection.
Brake usage: smooth, steady pressure — no riding or pumping the brake.
Lane usage: stay off curbs and lane markings, stop behind stop lines, and move to the right-most lane when it's clear.
Steering: both hands on the wheel except while shifting.
Regular traffic checks: mirrors and traffic checked constantly, especially at and through intersections.
Turn signals: used at the right time, held through the maneuver, and canceled afterward.

title: Test Day, Licensing & the One-Week Plan
examFocus: Test-day strategy, Florida-specific rules, and your 1-week study plan
summary: Exact test structure and passing scores, the manual-vs-automatic E restriction, CLP/ELDT rules, Florida test-day procedures, and a day-by-day plan to pass the written tests in one week.

topics.heading: The three written tests you'll take (Class A)
bullets: General Knowledge: 50 questions, need 40 right (80%). Taken by every CDL applicant.
Combination Vehicles: 20 questions, need 16 right (80%). Required for Class A.
Air Brakes: 25 questions, need 20 right (80%). Required if your truck has air brakes — a standard Class A tractor almost always does.
Endorsements add more tests: Hazmat 30 questions (need 24), Passenger / Tank / Doubles-Triples 20 questions each (need 16).
You get 2 attempts per test per day in Florida, and after a failed attempt you can review the exact questions you missed before retaking.
All knowledge tests are computerized and taken in person at a FLHSMV office or tax collector — there is no online testing.

topics.heading: Manual vs. Automatic — the E restriction
bullets: Test in an automatic (including an automated-manual / AMT like an Eaton UltraShift): you get the 'E' restriction — no manual transmission, ever.
Test in a manual: NO restriction — you can legally drive both automatic and manual trucks. This is the #1 reason to test in a manual if you can.
AMTs, semi-automatics, and any transmission that doesn't operate fully on the gear-shift-and-clutch principle count as 'automatic' for the restriction.
If you do get the E restriction, you can remove it later with a modified skills test in a manual truck — no ELDT required, and you don't redo the whole license.
Florida follows the federal rule: passing the skills test in an automatic-equipped vehicle must add the E restriction.

topics.heading: CLP, ELDT & the 14-day rule
bullets: Your CLP (Commercial Learner's Permit) is valid about 12 months, and you must hold it 14 days before taking the skills test.
Since February 7, 2022, first-time CDL applicants MUST complete Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) — theory, range, and road — from an FMCSA-registered provider before the skills test.
ELDT is verified electronically by FLHSMV, so you can't skip it or fake it. Get your CLP and start ELDT right away — it runs in parallel with your written-test study.
The knowledge tests are the fast part: a focused week of drilling practice tests is plenty to pass all three.
Your written-test passing scores stay valid for 1 year — that's your window to finish ELDT and pass the skills test.

topics.heading: The skills test (third-party, three parts)
bullets: Part 1 Pre-trip inspection: point to or touch, name, and explain every item. Florida uses the 7-step method.
Part 2 Basic control: Florida's exercises are Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing.
Part 3 On-road driving: turns, intersections, rail crossings, grades, and lane discipline.
Fail the pre-trip and you redo ALL THREE parts — FLHSMV asked FMCSA for an exemption and was denied in 2024. Pre-trip is the highest-stakes segment.
Florida uses state-contracted third-party test sites; Class A skills tests typically run $300–$500 and are paid directly to the tester.
The test vehicle must be a truck-tractor/semi-trailer combo with GCWR 26,001+ lbs and trailer GVWR over 10,000 lbs, with no labeled or marked components.

topics.heading: Florida test-day rules
bullets: Bring: valid Florida Class E license, Social Security number, proof of residency, DOT medical card, and your self-certification (interstate vs intrastate).
Under 21? You get the K restriction — intrastate only. Interstate driving and hazmat both require 21.
Knowledge tests are offered in multiple languages and can be taken orally in English or Spanish — but the Hazmat test is English-only.
Skills tests are English-only, and interpreters are prohibited for all tests.
Retest fees: $10 written, $20 skills. Initial CDL $75 plus $7 per endorsement, with a $6.25 service fee at tax collector offices.
There is no traffic-school point avoidance for CDL holders in Florida — convictions go straight on your record.

topics.heading: The one-week written-test plan
bullets: Day 1: Skim handbook Sections 1–3 + 11, take 2 General Knowledge practice tests, and log every miss by topic.
Day 2: Drill 4–6 General Knowledge tests until you hit 100% twice on two different sites; flashcard your misses.
Day 3: Air Brakes day — write the pressure ladder 20 times (125 cut-out / 100 cut-in / 55 warning / 20–45 spring brakes; 2-3-3-4 leak rates).
Day 4: Combination Vehicles — coupling/uncoupling steps, red vs blue lines, hand valve, fifth wheel, off-tracking.
Day 5: Full simulation — all three tests back-to-back, timed; book your FLHSMV appointment and start ELDT paperwork.
Day 6: Pre-trip script day — memorize the 7-step walk-around and say it out loud; re-take Air Brakes + Combination tests.
Day 7 (test day): One final pass of each practice test in the morning, arrive early, and use your 2 attempts if needed.
The night before: sleep. The morning of: caffeine, breakfast, and review your saved mistake list — not new material.

topics.heading: The trick numbers to drill (most-missed)
bullets: Air brakes: 125 psi governor cut-out, 100 psi cut-in, 55 psi low-air warning (or one-half governor cut-out on older vehicles), 20–45 psi spring brakes.
Leak rates: 2 psi/min single / 3 psi/min combo with brakes released; 3 psi/min single / 4 psi/min combo with the foot brake held.
Tread: 4/32 inch on steering tires, 2/32 inch on all others.
Following distance: 1 second per 10 feet of vehicle length under 40 mph, +1 second over 40 mph. A 40-ft truck needs 4 seconds; at 55 mph it's 5 seconds.
Stopping: 419 feet total at 55 mph; doubling your speed quadruples stopping distance.
Rail crossings: stop 15–50 feet from the nearest rail; a tractor-trailer needs about 14 seconds to clear a single track.
Red glad hand = emergency/supply line; blue = service line.
Cargo: re-check within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or 3 hours.

quiz.q: How many questions are on the Florida General Knowledge CDL test?
How many correct answers do you need to pass the 50-question General Knowledge test?
A Class A applicant must pass which three knowledge tests?
options: General Knowledge, Combination Vehicles, Air Brakes

quiz.q: How many questions are on the Combination Vehicles test, and how many do you need correct?
If you skip or fail the Air Brakes knowledge test, what restriction goes on your CDL?
options: L - No air brake equipped CMV
quiz.explain: If you do not take or fail the air brake component of the knowledge test (or test in a vehicle without air brakes), the 'L' restriction is placed on your license - no air brake equipped CMV.

quiz.q: What happens if you take the skills test in an automatic transmission truck?
options: You get the E restriction (no manual transmission)
You must retake the written test

quiz.q: For the E restriction, an automated manual transmission (AMT) like an Eaton UltraShift counts as:
options: A manual only if you double-clutch

quiz.q: You already have a CDL with the E restriction. To remove it you must:
options: Retake all knowledge tests and ELDT
Pass a modified skills test in a manual truck
Wait 3 years with a clean record
Take a written manual-transmission test only

quiz.q: How long must you hold your Florida CLP before taking the skills test?
What is ELDT and when is it required?
options: A written test you take online
Entry-Level Driver Training from an FMCSA-registered provider, required before your first skills test

quiz.q: How many attempts per test do you get in a single day in Florida?
You fail the pre-trip inspection portion of the skills test. What happens?
options: You redo all three skills segments
You redo the road test only

quiz.q: Which exercise is part of Florida's basic control skills test?
A driver self-certifies as intrastate-only. What restriction applies?
How many correct answers do you need on the 25-question Air Brakes test?
quiz.explain: You need 20 out of 25 (80%) correct on the Air Brakes knowledge test to pass.

quiz.q: What's the most important reason to take your Class A skills test in a manual transmission truck?
options: You avoid the E restriction and can legally drive both manual and automatic trucks
Manual trucks are cheaper to rent

title: Test Your Knowledge - All Handbook Review Questions
examFocus: Every 'Test Your Knowledge' review question from the official handbook, consolidated into one comprehensive module
summary: Every 'Test Your Knowledge' question from the official Florida CDL handbook, collected into a single comprehensive review module covering vehicle inspection, driving safely, cargo, passengers, air brakes, combination vehicles, doubles/triples, tanks, hazardous materials, and school buses.

topics.heading: How to use this module
bullets: This module pulls together ALL of the 'Test Your Knowledge' review questions found at the end of each section of the official Florida CDL handbook.
These are the exact questions the handbook says may be on your test: 'If you can't answer them all, re-read the section.'
Work through each topic area, and if you miss any, go back and re-read the corresponding handbook section before retaking the quiz.
This is a great final review before your General Knowledge, Air Brakes, and Combination Vehicles written tests.

quiz.q: What is the most important reason for doing a pre-trip vehicle inspection?
options: Safety for yourself and for other road users
To find out the fuel level
quiz.explain: Safety is the most important reason to inspect your vehicle - safety for yourself and for other road users.

quiz.q: What things should you check during a trip?
options: Gauges, your senses, and critical items when you stop (tires, brakes, lights, cargo securement)
quiz.explain: During a trip watch gauges, use your senses (look, listen, smell, feel), and check critical items when you stop: tires, brakes, lights, connections, and cargo.

quiz.q: Name some key steering system parts.
options: Tie rod, spindle, and pitman arm
Leaf spring, frame, and torque rod
quiz.explain: Important steering system parts include the steering wheel, steering shaft, tie rod, spindle, and pitman arm.

quiz.q: Name some suspension system defects.
options: Cracked or broken spring hangers, leaking shock absorbers, and broken leaves in the leaf spring
quiz.explain: Suspension defects include cracked or broken spring hangers, leaking shock absorbers, and broken leaves in the leaf spring.

quiz.q: What three kinds of emergency equipment must you have?
options: Fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (or circuit breakers), and warning devices (reflective triangles)
First aid kit, flares, and water
Jack, lug wrench, and spare tire
CB radio, fire extinguisher, and blanket
quiz.explain: You must carry a fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless you have circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles (three reflective triangles).

quiz.q: What is the minimum tread depth for front tires? For other tires?
options: 4/32 inch on front tires, 2/32 inch on all other tires
quiz.explain: Front (steering) tires need at least 4/32 inch tread depth; all other tires need at least 2/32 inch.

quiz.q: Name some things you should check on the front of your vehicle during the walk-around inspection.
options: Headlights, turn signals, windshield wipers, mirrors, tires, and the steering mechanism
quiz.explain: On the front of the vehicle during walk-around, check headlights, turn signals, windshield wipers and washer, mirrors, tires, and the steering linkage.

quiz.q: What should wheel bearing seals be checked for?
quiz.explain: Check wheel bearing seals for leaks - look for moisture around the seal and drops or a puddle underneath.

quiz.q: How many red reflective triangles should you carry?
quiz.explain: You must carry three red reflective triangles (or six fusees or three liquid-burning flares) for warning parked vehicles.

quiz.q: How do you test hydraulic brakes for leaks?
options: Pump the brake pedal three times and apply firm pressure for 5 seconds; the pedal should not move
Hold the brake down for 5 seconds and listen
Move forward and step on the brake hard
Pump the pedal five times for 3 seconds
quiz.explain: To test hydraulic brakes for leaks, pump the brake pedal three times, hold firm pressure for 5 seconds; the pedal should not move.

quiz.q: Why put the starter switch key in your pocket during the vehicle inspection?
options: So someone cannot start and move the truck while you are inspecting it
quiz.explain: Put the key in your pocket during the pre-trip so someone (like a co-driver) cannot start the vehicle and accidentally injure you.

quiz.q: Why should you back toward the driver's side?
options: So you can see better and avoid hitting something you cannot see
quiz.explain: Back toward the driver's side whenever possible so you can see the way you are going and avoid problems you cannot see.

quiz.q: If stopped on a hill, how can you start moving without rolling back?
options: Partly engage the clutch before you take your right foot off the brake
Increase RPMs and release the clutch quickly
quiz.explain: Partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake so the vehicle starts forward instead of rolling back on a hill.

quiz.q: When backing, why is it important to use a helper?
options: To help you see backing areas you cannot see from the cab and to guide you safely
quiz.explain: A helper guides you because you cannot see all backing areas from the cab. Agree on hand signals beforehand.

quiz.q: What's the most important hand signal that you and the helper should agree on?
quiz.explain: The stop signal is the most important to agree on because a misunderstanding could cause a crash.

quiz.q: What are the two special conditions where you should downshift?
options: Before starting down a hill and before entering a curve
Before starting up a hill and before parking
In intersections and at stop signs
When it rains and when it is dark
quiz.explain: You should downshift before starting down a hill and before entering a curve so you have engine braking and control.

quiz.q: When should you downshift automatic transmissions?
options: Before starting down a hill or curve, using the lower gear selector
quiz.explain: Downshift automatics before starting down a hill or entering a curve using the proper lower gear selector.

quiz.q: Retarders keep you from skidding when the road is slippery. True or False?
quiz.explain: False. Retarders can cause the drive wheels to skid when the road is slippery, especially in rain, snow, or ice.

quiz.q: What are the two ways to know when to shift?
quiz.explain: Know when to shift by engine speed (the RPM range for each gear) and by road speed.

quiz.q: How far ahead does the manual say you should look?
options: At least 12 to 15 seconds ahead (about one city block at low speed, a quarter mile at highway speed)
quiz.explain: Look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead - about one city block at low speed and a quarter mile at highway speed.

quiz.q: What are two main things to look for ahead?
quiz.explain: The two main things to look ahead for are other vehicles (which can cause hazards) and traffic signs and signals (which require action).

quiz.q: What's your most important way to see the sides and rear of your vehicle?
quiz.explain: Mirrors are the best and most important way to see the sides and rear of your CMV.

quiz.q: What does 'communicating' mean in safe driving?
options: Letting others know you are there by using turn signals, four-way flashers, and the horn
quiz.explain: Communicating means letting others know you are there and what you plan to do by using turn signals, four-way flashers, and the horn.

quiz.q: Where should you place reflectors when stopped on a divided highway?
options: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic
quiz.explain: On a one-way or divided highway place reflective triangles at 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic.

quiz.q: What three things add up to total stopping distance?
options: Perception distance + reaction distance + braking distance
quiz.explain: Total stopping distance = perception distance + reaction distance + braking distance.

quiz.q: If you go twice as fast, will your stopping distance increase by two or four times?
quiz.explain: Doubling your speed increases your stopping distance by about four times (it rises with the square of speed).

quiz.q: Empty trucks have the best braking. True or False?
quiz.explain: False. Empty trucks have less traction on the rear and can lock up more easily, making them harder to control when stopping.

quiz.q: What is hydroplaning?
options: When tires lose contact with the road and ride on a film of water, so you lose steering and braking
quiz.explain: Hydroplaning is when the tires ride on a film of water and lose contact with the road, so you lose steering and braking control.

quiz.q: What is 'black ice'?
options: A thin, nearly invisible coating of ice on the road that looks wet and is very slippery
quiz.explain: Black ice is a thin, nearly invisible layer of ice that makes the road look wet. It is very slippery and hard to see.

quiz.q: How do you find out how many seconds of following distance space you have?
options: Pick a fixed object ahead and count the seconds from when the vehicle ahead passes it until you pass it
Use a stopwatch on a mile marker
quiz.explain: Pick a fixed object ahead (shadow or landmark). Count the seconds from when the vehicle ahead passes it until you pass it - that is your following distance in seconds.

quiz.q: If you are driving a 30-foot vehicle at 55 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you allow?
options: At least 4 seconds (1 second per 10 feet + 1 second for speed over 40 mph)
quiz.explain: At 55 mph (>40 mph) with a 30-foot vehicle: 3 seconds (1 per 10 ft) + 1 second = 4 seconds of following distance.

quiz.q: You should decrease your following distance if somebody is following you too closely. True or False?
options: False - you should increase following distance to be able to stop more smoothly
quiz.explain: False. If someone follows too closely, increase your following distance so you can stop more gradually and avoid being rear-ended.

quiz.q: If you swing wide to the left before turning right, another driver may try to pass you on the right. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. If you swing wide to the left, another driver may try to pass on the right while you are turning. Turn with the rear as close to the curb as possible.

quiz.q: What is a hazard?
options: Any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger (something you must plan for)
quiz.explain: A hazard is any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger - something you must see, plan for, and respond to.

quiz.q: Why make emergency plans when you see a hazard?
options: To give you more time to act and avoid sudden braking or swerving that causes crashes
quiz.explain: Planning ahead when you spot a hazard gives you more time to act smoothly, avoiding sudden braking or swerving that is more likely to cause a crash.

quiz.q: What are some tips to follow so you won't become a distracted driver?
options: Finish phone calls and eating before driving, keep your attention on the road, and avoid non-driving activities
quiz.explain: Finish calls, eating, or other activities before driving. Keep your full attention on the driving task and never text or hold a phone while driving.

quiz.q: How do you use in-vehicle communications equipment cautiously?
options: Pull over to a safe place before using a phone or CB; never text or dial while driving
Use it only on the highway
quiz.explain: You may not hold a mobile phone to talk, dial by pressing more than one button, or text while driving. Pull over safely to use communications equipment.

quiz.q: How do you recognize a distracted driver?
options: Vehicles drifting, swerving, slowing and speeding up erratically, and delayed reactions
A driver who stays in one lane
A driver who looks in mirrors
quiz.explain: Distracted drivers may drift out of lane, swerve, slow and speed up erratically, and react late to traffic or lights.

quiz.q: What is the difference between aggressive driving and road rage?
options: Road rage is driving with the intent to cause harm or assault; aggressive driving is dangerous, pushy driving without that intent
quiz.explain: Aggressive driving is dangerous, pushy behavior that can cause crashes. Road rage is operating a vehicle with intent to harm someone or assault them.

quiz.q: What should you do when confronted with an aggressive driver?
options: Ignore rude gestures, avoid eye contact, do not react, and call the police if you can safely do so
quiz.explain: Do not give the aggressive driver the confrontation they want. Ignore the behavior, avoid eye contact, seek safety, and call police if safe to do so.

quiz.q: What are some things you can do to reduce your stress before and while you drive?
options: Give yourself plenty of time, keep a routine, and stay calm and focused on safe driving
quiz.explain: Reduce stress by allowing plenty of time, keeping a consistent routine, being courteous, and staying calm and focused - this also keeps you safer.

quiz.q: You should use low beams whenever you can. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. High beams can blind other drivers and reduce your vision as the light reflects back. Use low beams whenever possible.

quiz.q: What should you do before you drive if you are drowsy?
options: Sleep before you drive - never start a trip when drowsy
quiz.explain: If you are drowsy, sleep before driving. You cannot rely on coffee, fresh air, or radio to keep you alert.

quiz.q: What effects can wet brakes cause? How can you avoid these problems?
options: Wet brakes apply unevenly, work weakly, or grab; avoid them by drying with light brake pressure and driving carefully through water
quiz.explain: Wet brakes may apply unevenly, work weakly, or grab. After going through water, use light brake pressure to dry them and slow down.

quiz.q: You should let air out of hot tires so the pressure goes back to normal. True or False?
options: False - hot tires should not be bled; pressure rises with heat and is normal
quiz.explain: False. Do not let air out of hot tires. Tire pressure increases with heat normally; bleeding them while hot can cause underinflation problems.

quiz.q: You can safely remove the radiator cap as long as the engine isn't overheated. True or False?
options: False - the system must cool completely and you should still be careful of pressure and steam
Only if there is no overflow
quiz.explain: False. Even if the engine is not overheated, the cooling system holds pressure and hot steam. Let it cool completely and remove the cap carefully.

quiz.q: What factors determine your selection of a 'safe' speed when going down a long, steep downgrade?
options: Total weight of the vehicle and cargo, length of the grade, steepness, road conditions, and weather
quiz.explain: Select a safe speed based on total weight and cargo, length and steepness of the grade, road conditions, and weather.

quiz.q: Why should you be in the proper gear before starting down a hill?
options: Because you will not be able to shift into a lower gear once your speed builds up
Because the clutch needs to be warm
quiz.explain: You cannot downshift into a lower gear once speed builds up going downhill, and you could lose all engine braking effect.

quiz.q: Describe the proper braking technique when going down a long, steep downgrade.
options: Use the engine braking effect as the principal control; apply brakes to slow about 5 mph below your safe speed, then release and repeat
quiz.explain: Use engine braking as the principal control. Apply brakes just enough to feel a slowdown, reduce about 5 mph below safe speed, release, and repeat.

quiz.q: What type of vehicles can get stuck on a railroad-highway crossing?
options: Low-slung units (lowboy, car carrier, moving van, possum-belly livestock trailer)
quiz.explain: Low-slung units and single-axle tractors with long trailers can hang up on raised railroad crossings.

quiz.q: How long does it take for a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a double track?
quiz.explain: It takes a tractor-trailer at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.

quiz.q: Stopping is not always the safest thing to do in an emergency. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. You can often turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop. Stopping is not always the safest action.

quiz.q: What are some advantages of going right instead of left around an obstacle?
options: Avoids oncoming traffic and a head-on collision; the shoulder is usually clear
quiz.explain: Going right avoids forcing anyone into opposing traffic and a head-on collision. No one is likely to be driving on the shoulder.

quiz.q: What is an 'escape ramp'?
options: A long bed of loose, soft material to slow and stop a runaway vehicle, sometimes with an upgrade
quiz.explain: An escape ramp is a long bed of loose material used to stop a runaway vehicle, sometimes combined with an upgrade.

quiz.q: If a tire blows out, you should put the brakes on hard to stop quickly. True or False?
options: False - hold the wheel firmly and stay off the brake until you slow down, then brake gently
quiz.explain: False. Braking hard after a blowout can cause loss of control. Hold the wheel firmly and stay off the brake until the vehicle slows.

quiz.q: How do you know if your vehicle has antilock brakes?
options: A yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel (or on the left side of a trailer)
quiz.explain: Vehicles with ABS have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel; trailers have one on the left side near the front or rear corner.

quiz.q: What is the proper braking technique when driving a vehicle with antilock brakes?
options: Brake the same way you always have, using only the force needed; in an emergency with ABS on all axles you can fully apply the brakes
quiz.explain: With ABS, brake normally. Do not pump - ABS only works with steady pressure. In an emergency with ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes.

quiz.q: How do antilock brakes help you?
options: They keep wheels from locking so you maintain steering control and avoid skids/jackknifes
quiz.explain: ABS keeps wheels from locking during hard braking so you maintain steering control and avoid brake-induced skids or jackknifes.

quiz.q: What are some things to do at an accident scene to prevent another accident?
options: Get the vehicle off the road if possible, turn on flashers, and set out reflective triangles
quiz.explain: To protect the area, move vehicles off the road if possible, turn on flashers, and set out reflective triangles to warn traffic.

quiz.q: Name two causes of tire fires.
options: Underinflated tires and dual tires that touch
quiz.explain: Two causes of tire fires are underinflated tires and dual tires that touch each other.

quiz.q: What kinds of fires is a B:C extinguisher not good for?
options: Ordinary combustible fires (Class A) such as wood, paper, and cloth
quiz.explain: A B:C extinguisher is for electrical and flammable-liquid fires, not for ordinary combustible (Class A) fires like wood, paper, and cloth.

quiz.q: When using your extinguisher, should you get as close as possible to the fire?
options: No - stand at a safe distance and aim at the base of the fire
quiz.explain: Stand at a safe distance and aim at the base of the fire. Do not get closer than necessary, as heat and fumes are dangerous.

quiz.q: Name some causes of vehicle fires.
options: Electrical shorts, fuel leaks, overheated brakes, and poor maintenance
quiz.explain: Vehicle fires can be caused by electrical shorts, fuel and oil leaks, overheated brakes and tires, and poor maintenance.

quiz.q: Common medicines for colds can make you sleepy. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. Many cold and allergy medicines cause drowsiness. Read labels and never drive if a medicine makes you sleepy.

quiz.q: Coffee and a little fresh air will help a drinker sober up. True or False?
options: False - only time clears alcohol from the bloodstream
quiz.explain: False. Only time removes alcohol from the bloodstream. Coffee, fresh air, and cold showers do not sober a person up.

quiz.q: What is a hazardous materials placard?
options: A diamond-shaped sign on the vehicle that identifies hazardous materials and warns of the risk
quiz.explain: A placard is a diamond-shaped warning sign placed on the vehicle to identify hazardous materials being hauled.

quiz.q: Why are placards used?
options: To communicate the risk of the product being hauled
quiz.explain: Placards are used to communicate the risk of the hazardous material being transported.

quiz.q: What four things related to cargo are drivers responsible for?
options: Inspecting the cargo, recognizing overloads, making sure it is properly secured, and that it is distributed correctly
quiz.explain: Drivers are responsible for inspecting cargo, recognizing overloads, making sure it is properly secured, and ensuring it is distributed correctly.

quiz.q: How often must you stop while on the road to check your cargo?
options: Within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or every 3 hours, whichever comes first
quiz.explain: Check cargo within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or every 3 hours, whichever comes first.

quiz.q: How is Gross Combination Weight Rating different from Gross Combination Weight?
options: GCWR is the maximum weight the manufacturer allows (rating); GCW is the actual total weight of the loaded combination
GCW is a rating, GCWR is actual
quiz.explain: GCWR is the maximum weight the vehicle combination is rated to carry; GCW is the actual present weight of the loaded combination.

quiz.q: Name two situations where legal maximum weights may not be safe.
options: On steep downgrades and in poor weather/traction conditions
quiz.explain: A legal maximum-weight load may be unsafe on steep downgrades or in bad weather because it increases stopping distance and rollover risk.

quiz.q: What can happen if you don't have enough weight on the front axle?
options: The steering may be hard to control and the vehicle can oversteer dangerously
quiz.explain: Without enough weight on the front axle, the steering wheels can lose traction, making the vehicle hard to steer especially in curves.

quiz.q: What is the minimum number of tie-downs for any flatbed load?
quiz.explain: The minimum number of tie-downs is two, regardless of how small the load is.

quiz.q: What is the minimum number of tie-downs for a 20-foot load?
quiz.explain: Use at least one tie-down per 10 feet of load, with a minimum of two. A 20-foot load needs at least two.

quiz.q: Name the two basic reasons for covering cargo on an open bed.
options: To protect the cargo from weather and to prevent it from blowing or falling off
To improve fuel economy and looks
To keep it clean and dry only
quiz.explain: Cover cargo on an open bed to protect it from the weather and to prevent it from blowing away or falling off.

quiz.q: What must you check before transporting a sealed load?
options: That the load is properly balanced and secured in the vehicle
That the seal numbers match the bill
quiz.explain: With a sealed load you cannot look inside, but you are still responsible for ensuring the load is properly balanced and secured.

quiz.q: Name some things to check in the interior of a bus during a vehicle inspection.
options: Emergency exits, fire extinguisher, seats, floor, mirrors, and the parking brake
quiz.explain: In the bus interior, check emergency exits, fire extinguisher, seats, floor condition, mirrors, and that the parking brake works.

quiz.q: What are some hazardous materials you can transport by bus?
options: Small-arms ammunition, tear gas, and emergency hospital supplies (per the allowed exceptions)
quiz.explain: A bus may carry certain small quantities of materials like small-arms ammunition, tear gas, and hospital emergency supplies per exceptions.

quiz.q: What are some hazardous materials you can't transport by bus?
options: Explosives, flammable liquids, and most other hazardous materials not allowed by exceptions
quiz.explain: Buses generally may not carry explosives, flammable liquids, and most other hazardous materials unless a specific exception applies.

quiz.q: What is a standee line?
options: A line on the floor (or seats) in front of which standees may not pass in a bus
quiz.explain: The standee line marks the point in the bus floor (or seats) in front of which standing passengers may not go, keeping the driver's area clear.

quiz.q: Does it matter where you make a disruptive passenger get off the bus?
options: Yes - do so only at a safe place, never on the highway or where it is unsafe
quiz.explain: Make a disruptive passenger get off only at a safe place, never on the highway or where it would endanger the passenger or traffic.

quiz.q: How far from a railroad crossing should you stop?
options: Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
quiz.explain: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail so you can see the tracks clearly.

quiz.q: When must you stop before crossing a drawbridge?
options: When the drawbridge has no signal or has a sign requiring a stop
quiz.explain: Stop before crossing a drawbridge when it has no signal or has a sign requiring a stop; also obey any gates or signals.

quiz.q: Describe from memory the 'prohibited practices' listed in the manual.
options: No standing passengers past the standee line, no disruptive passengers left in unsafe areas, no moving students you believe may be seriously injured unless danger, and no driving when the bus is unsafe
quiz.explain: Prohibited practices include not letting standees past the standee line, not removing passengers in unsafe places, not moving a seriously injured student unless necessary, and not moving an unsafe bus.

quiz.q: The rear door of a transit bus has to be open to put on the parking brake. True or False?
quiz.explain: The statement is used to check if you know the parking brake: on many buses you set the parking brake with the rear door in a specific position, but the manual does not require the rear door to be open. (False - you should test the parking brake as directed.)

quiz.q: Why must air tanks be drained?
options: Water and compressor oil collect there and can freeze or coagulate and cause brake failure
quiz.explain: Air tanks collect water and compressor oil. If not drained, the water can freeze and cause brake failure.

quiz.q: What is a supply pressure gauge used for?
options: To show how much air pressure is in the tanks/supply system
quiz.explain: The supply pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is in the supply (storage) system.

quiz.q: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal (light and/or buzzer) that comes on before pressure drops below 55 psi.

quiz.q: What are spring brakes?
options: Powerful springs that apply the brakes automatically if air pressure is lost or drops too low
quiz.explain: Spring brakes use powerful springs that apply the brakes automatically when air pressure is lost or drops too low.

quiz.q: Front wheel brakes are good under all conditions. True or False?
quiz.explain: False. On slippery surfaces, locking the front wheels causes loss of steering control, so front brakes are not good under all conditions.

quiz.q: How do you know if your vehicle is equipped with antilock brakes?
options: A yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel (or left side of a trailer)
quiz.explain: Vehicles with ABS have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel; trailers have one on the left side near the front or rear corner.

quiz.q: What is a dual air brake system?
options: Two separate air brake systems with their own tanks and lines that use a single set of brake controls
Two systems that share the same tanks
A primary and backup that never work together
quiz.explain: A dual air brake system has two separate systems, each with its own tanks and lines, that use a single set of brake controls for safety.

quiz.q: What are the slack adjusters?
options: Part of the air brake system used to adjust the brakes to keep them safe
quiz.explain: Slack adjusters are part of the air brake system that allow you to adjust the brakes so they apply evenly.

quiz.q: How can you check slack adjusters?
options: Use gloves and pull hard on each slack adjuster; they should not have more than about one inch of 'give'
Press the brake pedal and listen
quiz.explain: Pull hard on each slack adjuster with gloves. If there is an inch or more of 'give', the brakes need adjustment.

quiz.q: How can you test the low pressure warning signal?
options: Shut the engine off, turn the key on, and step on and off the brake pedal; the warning must come on before pressure drops below 55 psi
quiz.explain: With the engine off and key on, pump the brake pedal. The low air pressure warning must activate before pressure drops below 55 psi.

quiz.q: How can you check that the spring brakes come on automatically?
options: Keep stepping on and off the brake pedal until pressure drops and the spring brakes deploy and the parking valve pops out
Push the pedal to the floor
quiz.explain: Step on and off the brake pedal to lower air pressure until the spring brakes come on automatically and the parking brake valve pops out.

quiz.q: What are the maximum leakage rates?
options: 3 psi in 1 minute (single), 4 psi in 1 minute (combination), 2 psi in 1 minute (air-over-hydraulic and trailers)
quiz.explain: Maximum leak rates: 3 psi/min single, 4 psi/min combination, 2 psi/min air-over-hydraulic and trailers.

quiz.q: Why should you be in the proper gear before starting down a hill?
options: You will not be able to shift into a lower gear once speed builds up
quiz.explain: You cannot downshift once speed builds up downhill, and you could lose all engine braking.

quiz.q: What factors can cause brakes to fade or fail?
options: Excessive service braking, not using engine braking enough, and brakes out of adjustment
quiz.explain: Brakes fade or fail from excess heat caused by excessive service braking, not relying on engine braking, or out-of-adjustment brakes.

quiz.q: The use of brakes on a long, steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. On long downgrades the engine braking effect is the principal control; the brakes only supplement it.

quiz.q: If you are away from your vehicle only a short time, you do not need to use the parking brake. True or False?
options: False - always use the parking brake even for a short time
quiz.explain: False. Always set the parking brake whenever you leave the vehicle, even briefly, and chock the wheels if needed.

quiz.q: How often should you drain air tanks?
options: At the end of each working day
At the end of each month
quiz.explain: Unless the vehicle has automatic drains, drain the air tanks at the end of each working day.

quiz.q: How should you brake when you drive a tractor-trailer combination with ABS?
options: Brake the same way you always have, using only the braking force necessary to stay in control
Press the pedal to the floor on every stop
quiz.explain: With ABS on a tractor-trailer, brake just as you always have - use only the braking force needed to stop safely and stay in control.

quiz.q: You still have normal brake functions if your ABS is not working. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. If ABS malfunctions you still have normal brakes. Drive normally but have the ABS serviced soon.

quiz.q: What two things are important to prevent rollover?
options: Keep cargo as close to the ground as possible and drive slowly around turns
quiz.explain: To prevent rollover, keep cargo as close to the ground as possible and drive slowly around turns.

quiz.q: When you turn suddenly while pulling doubles, which trailer is most likely to turn over?
quiz.explain: When turning suddenly with doubles, the last trailer is most likely to turn over because of rearward amplification (crack-the-whip effect).

quiz.q: Why should you not use the trailer hand brake to straighten out a jackknifing trailer?
options: The skid was caused by wheel lockup, and using the hand brake makes it worse by locking the trailer wheels more
quiz.explain: If the trailer is jackknifing because its wheels locked, applying the trailer hand brake locks them more and worsens the skid. Release the brakes instead.

quiz.q: What is off-tracking?
options: When the rear wheels follow a different (shorter) path than the front wheels in a turn
quiz.explain: Off-tracking is when the rear wheels go a different (shorter) path than the front wheels while turning a corner.

quiz.q: When you back a trailer, you should position your vehicle so you can back in a curved path to the driver's side. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. Back toward the driver's side in a curved path whenever possible so you can see the way you are going.

quiz.q: What type of trailers can get stuck on railroad-highway crossings?
options: Low-slung trailers (lowboy, car carrier, moving van, possum-belly livestock trailer)
quiz.explain: Low-slung trailers like lowboys, car carriers, moving vans, and possum-belly livestock trailers can hang up on raised rail crossings.

quiz.q: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?
options: Because of the danger of making the trailer skid
quiz.explain: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving because it may cause the trailer to skid.

quiz.q: Describe what the trailer air supply control does.
options: It supplies air to (and protects) the trailer and releases/keeps the trailer brakes when pulled out
quiz.explain: The trailer air supply control supplies air to the trailer air tanks and applies/releases the trailer emergency brakes. Pulling it out lets air out and applies the trailer brakes.

quiz.q: Describe what the service line is for.
options: It carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake to apply the trailer brakes
It supplies air to the tanks
quiz.explain: The service line carries air, controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand valve, that applies more or less pressure to the trailer brakes.

quiz.q: What is the emergency air line for?
options: It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the trailer emergency brakes
quiz.explain: The emergency air line has two purposes: it supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes.

quiz.q: Why should you use chocks when parking a trailer without spring brakes?
options: Because without spring brakes the trailer can roll if air leaks out of the emergency line
quiz.explain: A trailer without spring brakes can roll away if the emergency air line loses pressure. Use wheel chocks to keep it from moving.

quiz.q: Where are shut-off valves?
options: At the back of trailers (rear) where the air lines meet the glad hands
quiz.explain: Shut-off valves are at the back of trailers where the air lines connect to the glad hands.

quiz.q: What might happen if the trailer is too high when you try to couple?
options: The trailer may not couple correctly
quiz.explain: If the trailer is too high when coupling, the kingpin may not engage the fifth wheel correctly.

quiz.q: After coupling, how much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
options: No space - the trailer should be lying flat on the skid plate (no gap)
quiz.explain: After coupling there should be no gap between the upper and lower fifth wheel - the trailer should lie flat on the skid plate.

quiz.q: You should look into the back of the fifth wheel to see if it is locked onto the kingpin. True or False?
quiz.explain: True. Look into the back of the fifth wheel to confirm the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.

quiz.q: To drive you need to raise the landing gear only until it just lifts off the pavement. True or False?
options: False - you must raise the landing gear fully, as far as it will go
quiz.explain: False. Raise the landing gear fully (as far as it will go) before driving, not just until it lifts off the pavement.

quiz.q: How do you know if your trailer is equipped with antilock brakes?
options: A yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the left side of the trailer (front or rear corner)
quiz.explain: Trailers with ABS have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the left side, on the front or rear corner.

quiz.q: Which shut-off valves should be open and which closed?
options: All shut-off valves should be open except those at the back of the last trailer, which should be closed
quiz.explain: Open all shut-off valves except those at the back of the last trailer, which stay closed.

quiz.q: How can you test that air flows to all trailers?
options: Open the shut-off valves, build air pressure, and test the brakes on each trailer
quiz.explain: Open the shut-off valves, build up air pressure, and confirm the brakes on each trailer apply and release.

quiz.q: How can you test the tractor protection valve?
options: When tractor air pressure drops to about 25-40 psi, the valve should close automatically to keep air in the tractor
quiz.explain: The tractor protection valve closes automatically when tractor pressure drops to about 25-40 psi, protecting the tractor's air supply.

quiz.q: How can you test the trailer emergency brakes?
options: With the trailer connected and aired up, pull the trailer air supply control or disconnect the emergency line; the trailer brakes should apply automatically
quiz.explain: Operate the trailer air supply or disconnect the emergency line; the trailer emergency brakes should apply automatically.

quiz.q: How can you test the trailer service brakes?
options: With the trailer connected and aired up, apply the service brakes (foot pedal or hand valve) and confirm the trailer brakes apply and release
quiz.explain: Apply the service brakes with the foot pedal or hand valve and confirm the trailer brakes apply and release.

quiz.q: What is a converter dolly?
options: A chassis with one or two axles, a fifth wheel, and a drawbar used to couple a second or third trailer
quiz.explain: A converter dolly is a chassis with one or two axles, a fifth wheel, and a drawbar used to couple additional trailers behind the first.

quiz.q: Do converter dollies have spring brakes?
options: Yes, dollies built on or after April 1, 2001 are required to have spring brakes
quiz.explain: Converter dollies built on or after April 1, 2001 are required to have spring brakes.

quiz.q: What three methods can you use to secure a second trailer before coupling?
options: Chock the wheels, use the parking brake, or use the trailer's spring brakes
Park uphill, use hand brake, or block the hitch
quiz.explain: Secure a second trailer before coupling using wheel chocks, the parking brake, or the trailer's spring brakes.

quiz.q: How do you check to make sure trailer height is correct before coupling?
options: Make sure the trailer is low enough for the kingpin to engage the fifth wheel but high enough to clear the tractor nose
Raise it as high as it goes
quiz.explain: Set the trailer height so the kingpin engages the fifth wheel properly but the trailer clears the tractor nose during coupling.

quiz.q: What do you check when making a visual check of coupling?
options: The fifth wheel is locked on the kingpin, jaws and safety latch are closed, air lines connected, and landing gear raised
quiz.explain: Confirm the fifth wheel is locked on the kingpin with jaws and safety latch closed, air lines connected, and landing gear raised fully.

quiz.q: Why should you pull a dolly out from under a trailer before you disconnect it from the trailer in front?
options: So you can reach the shut-off valves and disconnect safely without damaging the dolly or trailer
quiz.explain: Pull the dolly out from under the trailer before disconnecting so you can access the shut-off valves and disconnect safely.

quiz.q: What should you check for when inspecting the converter dolly? The pintle hook?
options: Secure mounting, tires, air lines, glad hands, safety chains, and lights; and the pintle hook for wear, damage, and secure mount
quiz.explain: Inspect the dolly for secure mounting, tires, air lines, glad hands, safety chains, and lights. Check the pintle hook for wear or damage and a secure mount.

quiz.q: Should the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer be open or closed? On the first trailer of a set of doubles? On the middle trailer of a set of triples?
options: Closed on the rear of the last trailer; open on the first trailer of doubles and the middle trailer of triples
quiz.explain: All shut-off valves should be open except those at the rear of the last trailer, which should be closed.

quiz.q: How can you test that air flows to all trailers?
options: Open the shut-off valves, build air pressure, and test the brakes on each trailer
quiz.explain: Open the shut-off valves, build air pressure, and confirm the brakes on each trailer apply and release.

quiz.q: How do you know if your converter dolly is equipped with antilock brakes?
options: Dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 have an ABS lamp on the left side; older units may have the ECU and wheel speed sensor wires underneath
quiz.explain: Dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 must have an ABS lamp on the left side. For older units, look under for the ECU and wheel speed sensor wires.

quiz.q: How are bulkheads different than baffles?
options: Bulkheads are solid walls dividing the tank; baffles are partial walls with holes that slow liquid surge
Baffles are solid, bulkheads have holes
quiz.explain: Bulkheads are solid walls separating tank compartments. Baffles are partial walls with openings that slow the forward-backward surge of liquid.

quiz.q: Should a tank vehicle take curves, on ramps, or off ramps at the posted speed limits?
options: No - slow down well below posted limits because of surge and the high center of gravity
Yes, always at the posted limit
quiz.explain: A safe speed for most vehicles may be too fast for a tanker. Slow down before curves, ramps, and off ramps.

quiz.q: How are smooth bore tankers different to drive than those with baffles?
options: They have no baffles, so liquid surges more and they are harder to control
quiz.explain: Smooth bore tankers have no baffles, so liquid surges more freely and they are more difficult to control.

quiz.q: What three things determine how much liquid you can load?
options: Weight of the liquid, legal weight limits, and the space needed for expansion (outage)
quiz.explain: How much liquid you can load depends on the liquid's weight, the legal weight limit, and the room needed for expansion (outage).

quiz.q: What is outage?
options: The space left empty in a tank to allow liquid to expand as it warms
quiz.explain: Outage is the space left empty in a tank to allow the liquid room to expand as it warms.

quiz.q: How can you help control surge?
options: Keep the tank as full as possible (with proper outage) and avoid sudden stops and starts
quiz.explain: Surge is worst when the tank is partly full. Keep the tank reasonably full (with proper outage) and drive smoothly, avoiding sudden stops and starts.

quiz.q: What two reasons make special care necessary when driving tank vehicles?
options: The high center of gravity of the liquid and the surge that makes the vehicle hard to control
quiz.explain: Tank vehicles need special care because of the high center of gravity of the liquid and surge (liquid movement) that makes them hard to control.

quiz.q: Shippers package in order to (fill in the blank) the material.
quiz.explain: Shippers package hazardous materials in order to contain the material safely and prevent leaks.

quiz.q: Drivers placard their vehicle to (fill in the blank) the risk.
quiz.explain: Drivers display placards to communicate the risk of the hazardous materials being transported.

quiz.q: What three things do you need to know to decide which placards (if any) you need?
options: The hazard class, the amount being shipped, and whether the amount requires placards
quiz.explain: To decide which placards you need, know the hazard class of the material, the amount being shipped, and the rules for when placards are required.

quiz.q: A hazardous materials identification number must appear on the (fill in the blank) and on the (fill in the blank).
options: shipping paper (and package); it also appears on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging
the driver's log and fuel receipt
quiz.explain: The hazmat ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the package, and it must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

quiz.q: Where must you keep shipping papers describing hazardous materials?
options: Within easy reach of the driver's seat in a holder, or on the driver's seat when away from the vehicle
quiz.explain: Keep hazmat shipping papers within easy reach of the driver (in a holder), or on the driver's seat when you are away from the vehicle.

quiz.q: Around which hazard classes must you never smoke?
options: Flammable materials (e.g., Class 2 flammable gas and Class 3 flammable liquid) and explosives
quiz.explain: Never smoke around flammable materials such as Class 2 flammable gases and Class 3 flammable liquids (and near explosives).

quiz.q: Which three hazard classes should not be loaded into a trailer that has a heater/air conditioner unit?
options: Class 1 explosives, Class 2.1 flammable gases, and Class 3 flammable liquids
quiz.explain: Do not load Class 1 explosives, Class 2.1 flammable gases, or Class 3 flammable liquids into a trailer with a heater or air conditioner unit.

quiz.q: Should the floor liner required for Division 1.1 or 1.2 materials be stainless steel?
options: No - it should be non-metallic and nonsparking, not steel
Only if it is a tank
quiz.explain: The floor liner for Division 1.1 or 1.2 explosives should be non-metallic and nonsparking - not steel.

quiz.q: At the shipper's dock you're given a paper for 100 cartons of battery acid. You already have 100 pounds of dry Silver Cyanide on board. What precautions do you have to take?
options: Separate them because battery acid (a corrosive) reacts dangerously with Silver Cyanide (a poison); follow the segregation rules and never load them together where they can mix
Load them together to save space
quiz.explain: Battery acid (corrosive) and Silver Cyanide (poison) must be separated to prevent a dangerous reaction. Follow the segregation rules for incompatible materials.

quiz.q: Name a hazard class that uses transport indexes to determine the amount that can be loaded in a single vehicle.
quiz.explain: Radioactive materials (Class 7) use transport indexes to determine the maximum amount that can be loaded in a single vehicle.

quiz.q: What are cargo tanks?
options: Bulk packaging permanently attached to the vehicle that stay on when loading and unloading
quiz.explain: Cargo tanks are bulk packaging permanently attached to the vehicle; they remain on the vehicle when you load and unload.

quiz.q: How is a portable tank different from a cargo tank?
options: A portable tank is not permanently attached and is loaded/unloaded while off the vehicle, then put on for transport
quiz.explain: A portable tank is bulk packaging not permanently attached to the vehicle. It is loaded or unloaded while off the vehicle, then placed on a vehicle for transport.

quiz.q: Your engine runs a pump used during delivery of compressed gas. Should you turn off the engine before or after unhooking hoses after delivery?
options: After unhooking the hoses - keep the engine running until the hoses are disconnected so the system stays pressurized
quiz.explain: When your engine runs the pump for compressed gas delivery, keep it running until the hoses are unhooked so pressure is maintained, then turn it off.

quiz.q: If your placarded trailer has dual tires, how often should you check the tires?
options: Every 2 hours or every 100 miles, whichever comes first
At the start of the trip only
quiz.explain: Check the tires on a placarded trailer with dual tires every 2 hours or every 100 miles, whichever comes first.

quiz.q: What is a safe haven?
options: An approved site for parking vehicles transporting hazardous materials, authorized by FMCSA or local authorities
quiz.explain: A safe haven is an approved area authorized by FMCSA or local authorities for parking vehicles transporting hazardous materials.

quiz.q: How close to the traveled part of the roadway can you park with Division 1.2 or 1.3 materials?
options: You cannot park on the roadway
quiz.explain: Never park with Division 1.2 or 1.3 explosives within five feet of the traveled part of the road.

quiz.q: How close can you park to a bridge, tunnel, or building with the same load?
options: Within 300 feet (except for short periods needed for operation)
quiz.explain: Except for brief operating needs, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather, or open fire.

quiz.q: What type of fire extinguisher must placarded vehicles carry?
quiz.explain: Placarded vehicles must carry a B:C rated fire extinguisher of the required size for electrical and flammable-liquid fires.

quiz.q: You're hauling 100 pounds of Division 4.3 (dangerous when wet) materials. Do you need to stop before a railroad-highway crossing?
options: No - Division 4.3 is not a class that requires a mandatory stop
quiz.explain: Division 4.3 (dangerous when wet) is not among the hazmat classes requiring a mandatory stop before railroad crossings.

quiz.q: At a rest area you discover your hazardous materials shipments slowly leaking from the vehicle. There is no phone around. What should you do?
options: Follow your emergency plan and contact the shipper or carrier and emergency response as soon as possible
quiz.explain: If hazmat is leaking, follow your emergency plan and contact the shipper or carrier and emergency response. Never try to neutralize a leak unless trained.

quiz.q: Define the danger zone. How far does the danger zone extend around the bus?
options: About 10 feet from the front, sides, and rear of the bus
quiz.explain: The danger zone is the area around the bus where students are most at risk, extending about 10 feet from the front, sides, and rear.

quiz.q: What should you be able to see if the outside flat mirrors are adjusted properly? The outside convex mirrors? The crossover mirrors?
options: Flat mirrors: the side of the bus and rear tires; convex: the wider danger zone; crossover: the front bumper and ground in front of the bus
All mirrors show the same view
quiz.explain: Proper flat mirrors show the side of the bus and rear tires. Convex mirrors show the wider danger zone. Crossover mirrors show the front bumper and ground in front of the bus.

quiz.q: You are loading students along the route. When should you activate your alternating flashing amber warning lights?
options: At least 200 feet before the stop
quiz.explain: Activate the alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet before the stop so approaching drivers are warned.

quiz.q: You are unloading students along your route. Where should students walk to after exiting the bus?
options: To a point at least 10 feet in front of the bus, then to the left, and wait for the driver's signal before crossing
quiz.explain: After exiting, students should move at least 10 feet in front of the bus, out of the danger zone, and wait for the driver's signal before crossing.

quiz.q: After unloading at school, why should you walk through the bus?
options: To make sure no students are left on the bus or sleeping, and to check for hazards
quiz.explain: Walk through the bus after unloading to make sure no students are left on board and to check for hazards before driving away.

quiz.q: What position should students be in front of the bus before they cross the roadway?
options: At least 10 feet directly in front of the bus, in plain view of the driver and out of the danger zone
quiz.explain: Students should be at least 10 feet directly in front of the bus, out of the danger zone and in plain view of the driver, before crossing.

quiz.q: Under what conditions must you evacuate the bus?
options: When there is danger of fire, when the bus is in danger from a train or other traffic, or when it is otherwise unsafe to remain
quiz.explain: Evacuate when there is danger of fire, when the bus is in danger from a train or other traffic, or when it is otherwise unsafe to remain in the bus.

quiz.q: How far from the nearest rail should you stop at a highway-rail crossing?
options: Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
quiz.explain: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail so you can see the tracks clearly.

quiz.q: What is a passive highway-rail crossing? Why should you be extra cautious at this type of crossing?
options: A crossing with no gates, lights, or bells - only signs. Be extra cautious because there is no signal to warn you, so you must look and listen
quiz.explain: A passive crossing has no active warning devices, only signs. Because there is no signal, you must slow down, look, and listen for trains.

quiz.q: How should you use your brakes if your vehicle is equipped with antilock brakes (ABS)?
options: Brake the same way you always have; don't pump - use firm steady pressure
quiz.explain: With ABS, brake normally with firm steady pressure. Do not pump, as this defeats ABS.
